normalized_source_spec.hypothesis: Broadened delayed equal-energy intervention still charges storage to ready, boots, keeps the loaded TX rail above output_v, retains the event via the passive-mechanical latch (capture survives any reset before TX), stays above the off threshold through TX, and completes the single 8-byte frame within the 100 ms deadline.

The intervention delivers the same 150 uJ but broadens/delays the source pulse into [0.07,0.11] s at 3.75 mW. The executable device.event_latch='passive-mechanical' selector captures the press at event_s=0 with zero stored energy and retains it across the unpowered interval; event_latch_scope is provenance and does not override the selector. Retention makes the late pulse viable: the device boots after harvesting eon=0.5*C*ready_v^2, then boot_delay+tx_duration later emits one 8-byte frame near 0.0987 s, before deadline_s=0.1 s. Qualifying energy budget: (deadline - start_s - boot_delay_s - tx_duration_s)*power_w*harvest_efficiency >= eon; here 9.11e-5 J > 8.624e-5 J so complete service is preserved (adopt/PASS). Under a volatile latch, shorter deadline, or later pulse the relation fails and the decision flips to retain.

With the executable device.event_latch='volatile' selector, a brownout reset clears the captured event. In the intervention the 40 uJ shunt at 0.012 s fires after the 0-0.008 s contact capture window and before TX (not before 0.045 s), draining stored energy below the off threshold; the volatile capture is cleared and cannot be re-captured because the contact window has closed, so no frame is transmitted. In the current design the shunt at 0.08 s fires only after TX completes (~0.047 s), so the volatile capture survives and complete service is preserved. Adopt only when the shunt-induced reset does not fall between capture and TX completion.

Complete service is preserved only if the relocated reset shunt does not brown out the device during the volatile retention interval (capture .. TX-complete). The executable selector device.event_latch='volatile' governs retention; the inherited event_latch_scope string (passive-mechanical persistence) is apparatus provenance and does NOT override it, so a brownout clears the captured flag. The event is captured inside contact [0,0.008s]; TX cannot start before tx_not_before=0.045s and completes at ~0.047s having emitted the 8-byte frame. CURRENT design puts the 40uJ shunt at 0.08s, i.e. after TX-complete, so the frame is already sent (1 frame received, service preserved => retain baseline). INTERVENTION moves the same 40uJ shunt to 0.012s: this is after contact closes (0.008s) but before TX (0.045s), dropping stored energy below off_v threshold, so the volatile captured flag is cleared and, because contact has ended, cannot be re-captured; the device never transmits (0 frames) => the intervention does NOT preserve complete service => retain, prediction FAIL. Service is preserved only when the shunt time lies outside (contact_end, tx_complete).

Series reconfiguration of the two equal storage capacitors (C=5.5uF, ESR=1.2ohm) does not preserve complete service: the usable stored-energy band C*(cap_voltage_max_v^2-off_v^2)/2 (about 21.0uJ) is smaller than the single-frame delivered energy output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s (28.8uJ), so no 8-byte frame can be completed within the deadline; retain the parallel configuration.

Series rewire C 22->5.5 uF, ESR 0.3->1.2 ohm; passive-mechanical latch keeps capture across resets, so capture is not the failure mode. Usable energy at the first legal TX opportunity is bounded by C*ready_v^2/2 - boot_j - C*off_v^2/2 = 21.56 - 5 - 8.91 = 7.65 uJ (no credit taken for the 1 ms boot-delay recharge), while the 2 ms, 8 mA TX at 1.8 V against 6.75 mW harvest nets about 15.7 uJ of drain; the loaded rail falls through off_v/output_v before tx-complete, each retry restarts with the same budget, and no 8-byte frame arrives inside the 100 ms deadline, so the intervention does not preserve complete service and is retained.

The series-reconfigured two-cell storage intervention preserves complete 8-byte event service only if the energy stored above the off/UVLO floor when the ready rail is first reached covers the net payload TX energy over tx_duration (output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s minus harvested power over the same interval), the loaded rail worst case at the ready threshold (ready_v - esr_ohm*tx_current_a) still meets output_v, and estimated charge-to-ready plus boot_delay plus tx_duration stay inside the service deadline; otherwise the TX transient drops the loaded rail below output_v and resets the node before the application body is framed, so retain.

Under frozen b-transient-behavior-v1 with a passive-mechanical latch already captured (event retention identical in current and intervention), the only mechanism that can change the outcome is the stored-energy buffer above the off_v brownout floor, whose size is set by capacitance_f. Series reconfiguration of the two-cell assembly (C=5.5uF, ESR=1.2ohm) instead of parallel (22uF, 0.3ohm) shrinks buffer=C/2*(ready_v^2-off_v^2) to ~12.65uJ minus boot_j 5uJ plus net harvest during boot_delay_s ~0.0066uJ => ~7.66uJ available, while one 2 ms frame needs tx_duration_s*(output_v*tx_current_a+idle_power_w-source power*harvest_efficiency)~15.7uJ. Criterion: adopt iff available>needed (2 ms tx completes, one unique 8-byte frame before deadline_s=0.1s); else the tx-transient brownout aborts the packet and service is incomplete (retain). Conditions: passive-mechanical latch, dt_s=1e-4, single 7.5mW segment ending 0.02s, tx_not_before_s=0. UNKNOWN residual: boot-step overshoot above E_on and the ESR loaded_v guard are not modelled, so near zero margin this proxy is conservative rather than exact.
